title: Governance: promote the CBSP21 v2 SCOPE stamp from convention to a prompt-level rule (CLAUDE.md)
intent: Give the reinstated CBSP21 v2 read-scope fence structural teeth. The response-level SCOPE stamp adopted in the RPMCC24/CBSP21 charter is currently a convention — a fence that depends on the responder choosing to run it, which is the exact social-contract failure mode that killed CBSP21 v1. This promotes it to prompt-level: a light rule in CLAUDE.md so the scope declaration is structurally expected, not optional. Deliberately kept to the weight of the one-line SCOPE stamp to avoid the over-specification failure mode (a heavy declaration ritual gets gamed/routed-around).
behavior_change: None (project-instruction addition). Adds a light expectation that answers drawn from a document/upload carry a one-line scope declaration. No code, no gate, no CI change.

diff_articulation.what_changed: CLAUDE.md: added a short 'Scope declaration (CBSP21 v2)' section after Overview — one rule line (state what was read, how much of the whole, what was not read; never present a partial read as complete; a one-line SCOPE: stamp suffices) plus a pointer to docs/governance/CBSP21_v2.md.
diff_articulation.why_not_redundant: Converts the CBSP21 v2 scope fence from an ignorable convention into a structurally-expected rule — the durable enforcement level named in the charter, and the fix for the original 2025 note's failure (it was optional, so it was ignored). Kept intentionally light: the charter warns that a heavy scope-declaration ritual is the over-specification failure mode, so this codifies the SCOPE one-liner weight and nothing more.
diff_articulation.ordering_note: References docs/governance/CBSP21_v2.md, which lands with the charter branch docs/rpmcc24-cbsp21-charter (23ddf98e). Merge that charter PR first so the pointer resolves on main; this PR is the durable-follow-up named in that charter.

commands_run: Docs/instruction-only change; no test suite affected.
Weight check: rule is 1 line + pointer, matching the SCOPE one-liner the charter prescribes (avoids over-specification).
